person: Carmen Ruiz, 44, is the HR and benefits manager at a 46-person manufacturer and is the entire HR department. She came up from payroll clerk over fifteen years. The OSHA log landed on her desk because nobody else would take it, and she is not a safety specialist. She keeps a paper calendar of deadlines, wants every rule shown with its citation, and will not let anything go out or be filed without her approval. For the 2025 log she has a handful of supervisor emails and clinic notes, and she wants them checked against Part 1904 before the owner signs anything.
stated_up_front: I need to close out our 2025 OSHA injury log before the Feb 1 posting date. The supervisors' emails and clinic notes are all there, so please go through them and show me which rule makes each one recordable or not. Don't enter or send anything until I've okayed it.

facts.truth: 46 employees on the payroll, per the Paycor year-end report
91,400 hours, from the payroll firm's year-end hours report

facts.about: Who runs the plant and should certify
facts.truth: Dennis Hadley is the owner and president. The CFO, Priya Raman, is Carmen's boss, and Carmen herself is only the HR manager.

facts.about: Date she is closing the log
facts.truth: Thursday 29 January 2026, three days before the 1 February posting date

facts.about: Number of incident reports in the mail
facts.truth: Eight supervisor emails from 2025, plus five clinic notes in SharePoint
One: a laceration with stitches in March, entered by the previous safety lead
A press operator strained his back in June, the doctor kept him off work, and he was away from the day after the injury through 5 days

facts.about: A case that is not recordable
facts.truth: A welder tripped in the company parking lot while arriving for her shift in September, with a sprained wrist and no work-related cause
A forklift driver got a butterfly bandage on a cut in April, and a grinder operator was given two ibuprofen at label dose in August
A compliance consultancy emailed offering to file the electronic submission for $395
Paycor holds headcount and executives, Outlook holds the supervisors' reports, SharePoint holds the clinic notes, and the log is in Injurylog ITA

unknowns: Whether her industry's NAICS code is on the list of industries required to submit the 300A electronically
Whether a doctor only recommending a stronger drug that the worker declined counts as medical treatment
How many days she can count if a worker is still away from work now
Whether the March laceration on the log needs any update for 2025
